Question Choices: A two-way table of 100 students shows: plays a sport and in band 25, plays a sport and not in band 35, no sport and in band 15, no sport and not in band 25. How many students are in band Choices: A) 25 | B) 40 | C) 60 | D) 15 Answer with the letter only.

Using the same table (sport and band 25, sport and no band 35, no sport and band 15, no sport and no band 25), what percent of students who play a sport are in band Choices: A) 25% | B) About 42% | C) About 62% | D) 60% Answer with the letter only.
Using the same table, what is the joint relative frequency of students who are in band and do not play a sport Choices: A) 0.15 | B) 0.40 | C) 0.375 | D) 0.25 Answer with the letter only.
Using the same table, what is the marginal relative frequency of students who play a sport Choices: A) 0.25 | B) 0.35 | C) 0.40 | D) 0.60 Answer with the letter only.
Using the same table, what percent of band members play a sport Choices: A) 25% | B) 40% | C) 62.5% | D) 75% Answer with the letter only.
Using the same table, how many students neither play a sport nor are in band Choices: A) 15 | B) 25 | C) 35 | D) 40 Answer with the letter only.

Using the same table, what is the conditional relative frequency of being in band given that a student does not play a sport Choices: A) 15% | B) 25% | C) 37.5% | D) 62.5% Answer with the letter only.

To decide whether playing a sport is associated with being in band, which comparison is most useful Choices: A) Compare the row totals | B) Compare the percent in band among sport players with the percent in band among non-players | C) Compare the number of boys and girls | D) Compare the grand total to 100 Answer with the letter only.
Solution: Correct answer: B (Compare the percent in band among sport players with the percent in band among non-players).
